transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen, Evan Park, Priya Singh (Redwood) — Liam O'Connor, Sara Mehta, Diego Alvarez, Hannah Cho, Ravi Patel (Aperture)
Shared artifacts: onboarding-runbook-v1 (link), security-pack.pdf (link), benchmark-template.xlsx (link)

Summary (auto): Align on pilot configuration, security requirements, and immediate next steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, AE. with me is Evan, our solutions engineer, and Priya from CS. 
[00:22] Liam O'Connor: Hey thanks. Liam here, chief eng. We'll kick off from our side — sara, diego, hannah and ravi are on. Excited to get this moving.
[00:40] Evan Park: Hey all. Quick note: we prepared two reference architectures. One is Redwood Hosted API for fast start, the other is Dedicated in your VPC with private networking. We'll walk trade-offs.
[01:05] Sara Mehta: Great. Two big constraints up front: data residency —  we need EU-only storage for token logs — and KMS integration for key management. also latency target for critical paths is <120ms p95.
[01:30] Maya Chen: Totally — noted. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; we'll attach the security doc after.
[01:52] Hannah Cho: You said KMS/HSM — do you do HSM on prem or just cloud HSM?
[02:10] Evan Park: Right now we integrate with major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google KMS). For HSM we have options with our Private deployment — can work through compliance review. There's sometimes terminology mismatch in the docs, sorry if ours says HSM but means managed keys.
[02:37] Ravi Patel: And SSO — we need SAML + SCIM for user provisioning. Also RBAC enforced at route/model level.
[02:55] Priya Singh: We support SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC policies are configurable in the Console. We'll send screenshots in the onboarding doc.
[03:12] Diego Alvarez: On the Dedicated option: curious about autoscaling. Our traffic is bursty during batch closes, so we need predictable throughput and quick burst capacity. How does dedicated handle scale?
[03:36] Evan Park: Dedicated has reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. The autoscaler uses a scaling-up grace window — you pick target concurrency and burst headroom. For bursts we also recommend prefix caching and warm KV cache to reduce cold-start latency.
[03:58] Liam O'Connor: When you say prefix caching, is that caching customer prompts? We have a lot of templated prompts so that could save costs.
[04:15] Evan Park: Yes, prefix caching for repeated prompts/contexts — reduces tokens sent to model and lowers cost. We'll show suggested caching rules after we see the prompt set.
[04:40] Sara Mehta: Ok. Pilot timeline — we're thinking 6 weeks to pilot, then decide. We want measurable success metrics — cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency, and QA pass rate on a prompt set.
[05:05] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. Typical pilot we see is 2-week integration + 2-week benchmark + 2-week live shadowing. But we can compress or extend based on your priorities.
[05:27] Hannah Cho: Could you run a cost comparison if we use quantized models vs full fp16? We worry about quality regressions.
[05:44] Evan Park: Yes — Redwood Optimize provides quantization recommendations per workload. We'll produce a delta estimate; quality checks will be part of the test plan.
[06:05] Diego Alvarez: Reliability question — if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, do you have automatic fallback to hosted? We might want that to avoid outages.
[06:22] Maya Chen: We do. Smart routing can failover to hosted API or to a lighter-weight model variant. There are controls to restrict fallback for compliance reasons, though, so we'll document options.
[06:42] Ravi Patel: If we fall back to hosted, how about data residency? That could violate our EU-only requirement.
[06:56] Evan Park: Good catch. Fallback across regions is policy-driven — we can disable fallback to non-EU endpoints or only allow fallback to other EU-hosted instances. We'll make that explicit in the runbook.
[07:15] Liam O'Connor: Ok. On security: checklist we need — SOC 2, encryption at rest/in transit, audit logs, SSO, data deletion guarantees. Can you confirm each?
[07:33] Priya Singh: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II, TLS for in-transit, rest encryption with customer-managed keys optional, detailed audit logs in Console, and data retention controls plus deletion API. We'll attach certified docs.
[07:55] Sara Mehta: Great — please include proof of SOC2 date ranges and audit firm in the packet.
[08:07] Maya Chen: Will do.
[08:20] (crosstalk)
[08:40] Diego Alvarez: For network setup, we require a dedicated peering or private link. How long to get Dedicated provisioned in our VPC?
[08:55] Evan Park: Provisioning depends on cloud region and approvals. Typical lead time 3–5 business days for infra, plus network setup with your infra team. There is a checklist we'll run through.
[09:18] Ravi Patel: Who drives the network changes on our side? We prefer to own the peering and provide a ticket to engineering.
[09:30] Maya Chen: That works — we'll provide the exact ports and CIDRs.
[09:45] Liam O'Connor: On observability — what telemetry do you expose? We need per-route latency, token-level cost, error rates, traces.
[09:58] Evan Park: Console provides per-model/route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, tracing hooks, and error analysis. We also export metrics to Prometheus/Grafana and can push logs to your SIEM.
[10:20] Sara Mehta: Can we get a short demo of the Console in the next week?
[10:28] Priya Singh: Yes — we'll schedule a 45-min demo; I'll propose slots after this call.
[10:38] Maya Chen: Back to pilot: we recommend starting with a small set of routes — maybe 5 templates — to validate latency and quality before expanding.
[10:50] Diego Alvarez: Agreed. We'll pick the 5 highest-priority flows and provide sample traffic distribution.
[11:05] Hannah Cho: Compliance has a question: will you retain any PII from prompts or logs by default? We need options for redaction and retention windows.
[11:20] Evan Park: Default logs contain minimal metadata and a hashed prompt excerpt; full prompt logging is opt-in. We have redaction tools and can run pre-processing to strip PII before it hits Redwood. We'll include guidance in the runbook.
[11:45] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. On the benchmark plan — we want latency under 120ms p95 for the critical path. How do you recommend we measure it?
[12:02] Evan Park: We'll provide a benchmark template; tests should be run from your client region against the Dedicated endpoint. We'll include warmup steps, concurrency ramp, and sample prompt set. Also recommend KV cache warming to simulate production.
[12:25] Ravi Patel: About costs — how do we estimate monthly for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[12:36] Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing — predictable commit-based contract plus unit cost for tokens. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing. We'll share a cost model and run numbers after you share expected QPS and token lengths.
[12:55] Sara Mehta: Do you offer discounts for multi-month commit?
[13:03] Maya Chen: Yes, we have reserved capacity discounts for 6–12 month commitments. We'll share a draft commercial outline.
[13:18] (brief pause)
[13:35] Diego Alvarez: Ok next: rollback and safety — if model rollout causes quality regressions, how do we handle automatic fallback and can we run A/B?
[13:49] Evan Park: We provide canary rollouts and A/B testing via the Console with automatic rollback triggers based on custom metrics e.g., latency, error rate, or specific evals on prompt sets.
[14:10] Hannah Cho: We want automated quality checks that run daily on a canonical prompt set — can Redwood do scheduled evals?
[14:22] Priya Singh: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports scheduled evals and alerts for regressions. We'll enable alerting to Slack or PagerDuty.
[14:38] Liam O'Connor: Two questions from procurement: contracting terms around data ownership and indemnity — can legal share a standard enterprise SOW?
[14:52] Maya Chen: Yes — our legal team has a standard enterprise SOW and DPA. I'll loop in our legal contact after this call.
[15:04] Sara Mehta: One more technical detail: do you support model pinning per-route? We need to pin a safety-filtered model for customer-facing flows.
[15:20] Evan Park: You can pin model versions per route; fallback policies can target compatible variants. We'll walk through model catalog entries in the demo.
[15:36] Diego Alvarez: On instrumentation — can we emit traces correlating request IDs back to our logs?
[15:50] Evan Park: Yes, we support passing request IDs and trace contexts; Console shows request-level traces and we can export logs to your ELK/SIEM.
[16:05] (longer segment skipped for brevity)
[20:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap before we open to questions: 1) Redwood will share security pack and runbook by 6/30. 2) Customer to provide prompt set and traffic profile by 7/2. 3) Evan will propose benchmark windows by 7/1. 4) Schedule dedicated provisioning meeting week of 7/6.
[20:22] Liam O'Connor: Confirmed. Also want a demo for the console and one deep-dive session for infra.
[20:35] Priya Singh: We'll send invites for both.
[21:00] Hannah Cho: Tiny nit — you mentioned audit logs retention. What's max retention? 90 days? 365?
[21:12] Evan Park: Default 90 days, longer retention available as an add-on. We'll include options and pricing.
[21:30] Sara Mehta: For the prompt redaction, is there client-side tooling?
[21:42] Evan Park: We have an SDK helper to run client-side redaction or you can integrate our pre-processing step in your pipeline.
[22:00] Liam O'Connor: Ok, decision to start with Dedicated pilot but lock fallback to EU-hosted only. Also, include a toggle to disable fallback for specific routes.
[22:18] Maya Chen: Noted — we'll document the fallback policies and route-level controls.
[22:35] Diego Alvarez: For benchmarks, we want to run two windows: an integration run and then a production-ish load run.
[22:48] Evan Park: We'll include that in the test plan.
[23:05] (crosstalk — lunch break jokes)
[23:30] Priya Singh: Action items again: Maya will share security pack; Evan benchmark plan; Diego sample prompts; Priya will schedule demo and provisioning meeting.
[23:52] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Our internal goal is to have the pilot start first week of July.
[24:05] Maya Chen: We'll aim for that. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links.
[24:20] (meeting ends)
